description:
FILED s473t6d (Opus, 2026-09-20), found by #1954's breaking-case probe
(`probes/p7.pl` row 17); PRE-EXISTING (identical on a `268d7e00` extraction).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):

    sub mk { return [1,2] }
    for (mk()) { print "ref=", ref($_), "\n" }

    perl: ref=ARRAY          (ONE iteration -- a sub returning one scalar)
    PCL:  ref=                (two iterations, $_ = 1 then 2)

MECHANISM: the #267 rule (a foreach list of single SCALAR operands emits
`(vector ...)` rather than going through `%p-flatten-for-list`) is decided
from the SIGIL, which is compile-time knowledge.  A sub call has no sigil:
`mk()` may return a list or one scalar, and at runtime a box wrapping a vector
is indistinguishable from an @array box -- the very ambiguity
`_foreach_single_scalar_p`'s comment records.  So this is NOT another arm in
that predicate; it needs the runtime to be able to tell a REFERENCE box from
an @array box, which is the `ref-kind` slot that was measured and REJECTED
(ruled s335).

WHAT WOULD DECIDE IT: `p-sub` already knows the call's CONTEXT.  A sub called
in the foreach list is called in LIST context, and what it returns is a LIST
of values; the loss is that a single returned REFERENCE is then spread.  The
honest shapes to measure before designing anything:

    sub one  { return [1,2] }            # one ref      -> 1 iteration
    sub many { return ([1],[2]) }        # two refs     -> 2 iterations
    sub arr  { my @a=(1,2); return @a }  # a real list  -> 2 iterations

`many` and `arr` already work; only `one` is wrong, and the three are
indistinguishable to the flattener.  The fix therefore lives in how a sub's
return VALUE carries its ref-ness -- the same question #1991 and #551 ask from
their own sides.

ROWS: no blessed row is behind it today (found by probe), but the shape is
everyday Perl (`for (get_config()) {...}`) and it is SILENT.
subject: SILENT WRONG: a foreach list containing a SUB CALL that returns a reference is FLATTENED -- `for (mk()) { ref $_ }` with `sub mk { [1,2] }` iterates the referent's elements
